items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Kaiser Marshall was playing with Fletcher... he come with this thing... Kaiser was a beautiful drummer. He fitted Fletcher's band like a glove. He used to tell everybody he was my brother.

ctx.x: : So you didn't use any sock cymbal then.

They hadn't invented them. I'm glad you asked me that. We were playing the Kentucky Club, they had two flat boards on the floor, just mashed them together, you know, step on them with that foot. So one day from my factory, the guy come to New York and Kaiser Marshall was playing with Fletcher, up the street at Roseland, so he come with this thing, high-hat, first time it come out and the guy brought it to me first.

He said 'We want you to play this and demonstrate this for us,' so man, 'I can't play that thing,' so he said 'It's easy.' He showed me, 'And your legs won't get tired.' Used to get tired patting that board, on the floor. So I took this damn thing and after a few tries, I begin to experiment with the thing, and I found out, I could do the same thing on the high-hat, that I could do on the snare drum.
